blocks.text: Built 1997; 22 units; Freehold Strata title; a 3-level building according to the strata directory. Current listings describe a 55+ community and a "well-cared-for boutique 22-unit building" backing onto Belhouse Park, a short walk to the Delbrook Community Recreation Centre, Mosquito Creek Trail and Westview shopping, with a club house, workshop, exercise centre, bike room and common courtyard; one listing states the pets position as "Cats OK" and the building description calls it pet friendly. The building directory states the strata bylaws include age restrictions, pets allowed and rentals allowed. The 55+ position is stated here as published — it is the one age-bylaw form BC law allows — and the filed bylaw wording should still be confirmed on the Form B. The directory also lists the amenities as Elevator, In Suite Laundry and Recreation Center.

The name and form are confirmed on an official District source: a District council report describes "the existing Delbrook Plaza, a mixed-use commercial/residential development, zoned CD38" immediately west and north of 3707 Delbrook Avenue. Listings for residential units at 3711 and 3721 Delbrook Avenue state Apartment/Condo sub-type, built 1988, wood-frame construction, and describe a two-level townhome-style apartment with only one shared wall that is pet-friendly, with 2 side-by-side parking stalls and a storage locker.

items.t: Delbrook is a confirmed District of North Vancouver neighbourhood name: one of the five distinct residential neighbourhoods (Delbrook, Norwood/Queens, Upper Delbrook, Carisbrooke and Braemar) inside the District's North Lonsdale–Delbrook planning area, around Delbrook Avenue and West Queens Road. District-wide land use is guided by the Official Community Plan, Bylaw 7900.

Where the condo stock actually concentrates: two small pockets only. Queensbrook sits on West Queens Road at the area's south-west edge near Westview, and Delbrook Plaza sits on Delbrook Avenue itself at the Evergreen Place end.

Nearby areas: Edgemont Village (west, across Mosquito Creek), Upper Delbrook and Braemar (north and east), Upper Lonsdale / Queensdale (east, along Lonsdale Avenue — Queensdale, on Lonsdale Avenue at Queens Road, is one of the District OCP's six Village Centres), and Norgate / Pemberton Heights (south, below West Queens Road toward Marine Drive).

Main streets and transit: West Queens Road is an east–west major arterial, and Delbrook Avenue is a two-lane minor arterial that transitions into Westview Drive south of West Queens Road and connects the surrounding residential areas to the Trans-Canada Highway (Highway 1). TransLink route 249 (Delbrook / Lonsdale Quay) runs via Westview Drive, Delbrook Avenue and Montroyal Boulevard to Lonsdale Quay, continuing as a 246 downtown trip; route 246 runs on Delbrook Avenue and route 232 runs on West Queens Road — direct buses toward downtown Vancouver, the SeaBus (12 minutes to Waterfront Station) and Phibbs Exchange respectively.

Anchors inside and beside the area: the Delbrook Community Recreation Centre, 851 West Queens Road (main pool, leisure pool and indoor racquet facilities), Delbrook Park on West Queens Road, and Westview Shopping Centre south of West Queens Road; the elementary schools beside the area are École Braemar Elementary, 3600 Mahon Avenue, and Carisbrooke Elementary, 510 Carisbrooke Road East, with Carson Graham Secondary, 2145 Jones Avenue, the secondary school south of the neighbourhood in the City.

items.t: Hazard permits: District OCP Bylaw 7900, Schedule B sets Development Permit Areas including Protection of the Natural Environment, Streamside Protection, Wildfire Hazard, Creek Hazard and Slope Hazard — Mission Creek borders the Delbrook Lands on the west and Mosquito Creek lies farther west, so creek-side Delbrook lots are exactly the lots these areas were written for. The District's landslide hazard work rests on its Landslide Risk Assessment, commissioned after the January 19, 2005 Berkley landslide in the District's east end; slope lots on Delbrook's upper streets should be checked against the District's hazard reporting rather than assumed clear.

items.t: The neighbourhood's recreation centre moved, and its old site is the development story. The current Delbrook Community Recreation Centre is at 851 West Queens Road; the former centre site at 600 West Queens Road (the Delbrook Lands, about 17,600 m²) is being redeveloped under Bylaws 8397–8399 into a neighbourhood park (northern portion) plus the four-storey rental and seniors-care building (southern portion) — a District-built project on District land, directed by Council on July 22, 2019.

The old Delbrook plan is repealed — do not rely on it. The former North Lonsdale–Delbrook Official Community Plan (Bylaw 6750, adopted 1995) named Delbrook as one of five neighbourhoods, but that plan is repealed and District OCP Bylaw 7900 now covers the area; a seller or agent quoting the 1995 plan's designations is quoting a dead bylaw.

Queensbrook's park is its front yard. Listings describe the 22-unit building as backing onto Belhouse Park and its tennis courts, a short walk to the recreation centre and the Mosquito Creek Trail — the amenity package for the area's only 55+ building is the park-and-trail network, not in-building facilities beyond its club house, workshop, exercise centre and courtyard.

items.t: District zoning and plan — the DISTRICT pair only: Official Community Plan Bylaw 7900 and Zoning Bylaw 3210. Section 525 (Bylaw 8799) states the R1 zone minimum lot is 4,000 m² with 30 m width and 34 m depth, and the R2 zone minimum lot is 660 m² with 18 m width and 34 m depth, with modifiers R2(S1) at 335 m² / 10 m, R2(S2) at 1,100 m² / 24 m and R2(S3) at 4,000 m² / 30 m; an R2 lot may hold one principal dwelling, one secondary suite and one coach house, and since June 2024 three units total are permitted on single-family zoned properties within the Urban Containment Boundary. The District's GEOweb SSMUH classification shows non-exempt lots potentially allowing up to 3 units at 280 m² or less, up to 4 units above 280 m², and up to 6 units above 280 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit bus stop. The former North Lonsdale–Delbrook Official Community Plan (Bylaw 6750, adopted 1995) is repealed — a seller quoting its designations is quoting a dead bylaw.

Hazard permit areas: District OCP Bylaw 7900, Schedule B sets Development Permit Areas including Protection of the Natural Environment, Streamside Protection, Wildfire Hazard, Creek Hazard and Slope Hazard — Mission Creek borders the Delbrook Lands on the west and Mosquito Creek lies farther west, so creek-side and upper-slope Delbrook lots are exactly the lots these areas were written for; check the District's GeoWeb hazard layers before pricing a renovation or rebuild.

items.t: The recreation centre inside the area is the real one; the famous lands are the old one. The Delbrook Community Recreation Centre at 851 West Queens Road — main pool, leisure pool and indoor racquet facilities — is operating inside the sub-area, while the former centre's lands at 600 West Queens Road are the redevelopment site. Buyers routinely merge the two addresses; they are different properties on the same road.

Queensbrook's 55+ status is in the District's own record, not just its marketing. A 2004 District council report states the 22 units at 678 W. Queens Road, built in 1997, were the only one of three sites designated in 1995 that actually redeveloped for 55+ housing, and a 1996 District report required a Housing Agreement "to ensure the project is occupied by seniors" — the designation has a paper trail most marketed "55+" buildings cannot produce.

The hospital and urgent care are in the City, minutes south: Lions Gate Hospital, 231 East 15th Street, serves the North Shore, and the North Vancouver Urgent and Primary Care Centre is at Suite 200, 221 West Esplanade — both Vancouver Coastal Health facilities in the City of North Vancouver serving this District neighbourhood.

items.t: Established bench lots: detached houses on R1 and R2 lots along Delbrook Avenue and its side streets — the R2 zone's stated intent is ground-oriented detached housing in the form of a house which may include a suite and be accompanied by a coach house. The bench street pattern is historic subdivision fabric — built lots, not a lot offering.

Lot character, as the District states it (Zoning Bylaw 3210, Section 525, Bylaw 8799): the R1 zone minimum lot is 4,000 m² with 30 m width and 34 m depth; the standard R2 zone minimum lot is 660 m² with 18 m width and 34 m depth; modifiers run R2(S1) at 335 m² / 10 m width, R2(S2) at 1,100 m² / 24 m and R2(S3) at 4,000 m² / 30 m. The zone on a single lot is confirmed through the District's GeoWeb. These are zone minimums, not a claim about any existing lot's size.

Serviced position: Delbrook's established streets sit inside the District's serviced urban system — District single-family utility fees in 2026 total $2,571.20, including water at $932.80 and sewer/drainage at $1,255.60. Parcel-level servicing detail, and any septic or well position for a specific lot: confirm the specific parcel with the District.
No ALR percentage split is stated — check any specific parcel on Agricultural Land Commission mapping.

This is a District-built rental, care and park project on District land — no lots are offered, no lot count or sale terms exist in the material read, and nothing here is carried as for-sale inventory.

items.t: OCP / Zoning — DISTRICT rulebook only: District of North Vancouver Official Community Plan, Bylaw 7900, and Zoning Bylaw 3210. The former North Lonsdale–Delbrook Official Community Plan (Bylaw 6750, adopted 1995), which named Delbrook as one of its five neighbourhoods, is repealed — Bylaw 7900 now covers the area.

Added units / SSMUH as the District states it: an R2 lot may hold one principal dwelling, one secondary suite and one coach house, and since June 2024 three units total are permitted on single-family zoned properties within the Urban Containment Boundary. The District's GeoWeb SSMUH classification shows non-exempt lots potentially allowing up to 3 units at 280 m² or less, up to 4 units above 280 m², and up to 6 units above 280 m² within 400 m of a frequent-transit bus stop — parcel-specific; run the lot in GeoWeb before pricing potential.

Hazards — Schedule B permit areas: District OCP Bylaw 7900, Schedule B sets Development Permit Areas including Protection of the Natural Environment, Streamside Protection, Wildfire Hazard, Creek Hazard and Slope Hazard — Mission Creek borders the Delbrook Lands on the west and Mosquito Creek lies farther west, so creek-side Delbrook lots are exactly the lots these areas were written for.

Hazards — landslide diligence: the District's landslide hazard work rests on its Landslide Risk Assessment, commissioned after the January 19, 2005 Berkley landslide in the District's east end; slope lots anywhere in the District, including Delbrook's upper streets, should be checked against the District's hazard reporting rather than assumed clear.

If a parcel is in the ALR: subdivision within the ALR requires ALC approval; ALR residences cannot be stratified. On ALR land the main house can be up to 500 m², a suite is allowed only inside it, and an extra residence can be up to 90 m² (186 m² on parcels over 40 ha). For farm class, BC Assessment looks for farm income of $10,000 a year on under 0.8 ha, $2,500 on 0.8 to 4 ha, and $2,500 plus 5% of the value of land over 4 ha; applications are due by October 31.

items.t: The board name covers two District neighbourhoods: District planning splits this bench into Delbrook and Upper Delbrook (two of the five neighbourhoods in the North Lonsdale–Delbrook planning area), while the board-style search name "Delbrook" covers both — a search, and a price comparison, run under the one name silently mixes the lower bench with the upper streets.

The old Delbrook plan is repealed law: the North Lonsdale–Delbrook Official Community Plan (Bylaw 6750, adopted 1995) that first named these five neighbourhoods no longer governs — District OCP Bylaw 7900 does.

The recreation centre moved, and its old site is the density story: the current Delbrook Community Recreation Centre at 851 West Queens Road is inside the area, while its former site at 600 West Queens Road becomes a park plus a four-storey rental and seniors' care building — the streetscape on Stanley Avenue and West Windsor Road changes with it, which is worth raising in pricing conversations on those streets.

Delbrook's transit is stronger than most District benches: routes 249, 246 and 232 give the area direct service to Lonsdale Quay / SeaBus, downtown Vancouver and Phibbs Exchange respectively on the area's own streets — worth naming route by route, because the SSMUH classification's 400 m frequent-transit test turns on exactly that geography.

faq.a: Two buildings: Queensbrook (678 West Queens Road, 22 units, built 1997, 55+) and the residential component of Delbrook Plaza (3711/3721 Delbrook Avenue, built 1988). Everything else in the neighbourhood is detached houses on R1/R2 lots, plus the coming non-market rental and seniors-care building at 600 West Queens Road, which is not purchasable.
faq.q: How many condos are there in Delbrook, really?

faq.a: It is marketed as a 55+ community and the directory records age restrictions, pets allowed and rentals allowed. A 55-or-older bylaw is the only age bylaw valid under Strata Property Act ss. 123.1/123.2, and the statutory exemptions cover legacy residents, live-in caregivers and, from May 1, 2023, younger spouses/partners and defined children — so a younger spouse is not automatically barred, but the filed bylaw wording governs and must be read on the Form B before writing.
faq.q: Is Queensbrook really 55+ — and what does that mean for a younger spouse?

faq.a: Queensbrook: the directory states pets allowed, and a current listing states "Cats OK" while the building description calls it pet friendly — confirm species/size wording on the Form B. Pet bylaws still bind, unlike rental bylaws.
faq.q: Can I have a pet at either building?

faq.a: No. The Delbrook Lands project is a District-led four-storey building with low-to-moderate-income rental housing and a seniors' care facility (reported as 86 affordable homes run by the non-profit Hollyburn Community Housing Society), plus a new neighbourhood park on the northern portion of the site. It changes the streetscape on Stanley Avenue and West Windsor Road, but there is no strata lot to purchase.
faq.q: Can I buy into the new building going up at 600 West Queens Road?

faq.a: The Form B package: the filed age-bylaw wording, the latest depreciation report (a 22-lot strata is inside the every-five-years, no-deferral-vote requirement), financials, the CRF balance against the 10%-of-operating-fund minimum contribution, and planned work. In a 22-unit building each owner carries roughly 1/22 of any special levy.
